diagnosis.what_happened: A 2-indicator latent factor composed of opposing subscales was fit, causing Heywood cases. Warnings were suppressed and invalid results were generated.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Suppressing R warnings allowed statistically inadmissible results (negative variances, beta > 1.0) to pass into final reports.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: The system should have strictly failed upon detecting Heywood cases, non-invertible matrices, or parameter boundaries exceeded.
diagnosis.rationale_why: SEM relies on matrix invertibility and valid bounds. Results from inadmissible matrices are mathematically meaningless.

desired_behavior: Enforcing a strict fail-closed mathematical admissibility gate requiring lavaan post-check verification, information matrix invertibility, zero negative variances, and all standardized betas <= 1.0 before any SEM results or chapter deliverables can pass validation.
generalization: Never proceed with SEM interpretation or artifact generation if Heywood cases or non-positive definite matrices occur.

evidence.threshold_value: Zero tolerance for mathematically inadmissible models.
